samples.summary: The three new HttpClient methods are never exercised — the whole client is mocked, so nothing verifies the real request URL/method/body (including `seg()` escaping) for browse/publish/use
samples.evidence: templates.test.ts:23-29 replaces `HttpClient` wholesale with a stub, so `browseTemplates`/`publishTemplate`/`useTemplate` in src/client/http-client.ts:1148-1176 never run in any test. The only URL assertions are the `--dry-run` previews (lines 149-158, 236-253, 303-313), which call the url.ts builders directly from the command, not through the client. The repo's convention for exactly this is packages/cli/test/http-client-paths.test.ts, which drives the REAL HttpClient with `fetch` stubbed and asserts escaped paths for the sibling browser route (`revokeApiKey`, line 76-81); no template equivalent was added (grep for 'template' across packages/cli/test matched only templates.test.ts). Consequence: if `publishTemplate` or `useTemplate` built its path without `seg()` or against the wrong route, or sent the body under the wrong key, every test here still passes while the preview keeps claiming 'the preview is the request'.

samples.summary: `templateBrowseParams` has no direct unit test; its empty-string-dropping branch is uncovered
samples.evidence: url.ts:128-136 drops values that are `undefined` or `''`. packages/cli/test/url.test.ts contains no template cases (grep for 'template' in packages/cli/test matched only templates.test.ts), and the command tests only reach the builder via the single workspace-scope dry-run at templates.test.ts:149-158, which exercises no empty value. An empty `--workspace`/`--tag` silently reaching the query as `tag=` (the DTO rejects it) would not be caught.

samples.summary: No dry-run/URL test for the public scope, which is the branch the diff's stated invariant (no workspaceId) is about
samples.evidence: The only preview assertion for list (templates.test.ts:149-158) uses the default workspace scope and asserts `scope=workspace&workspaceId=ws-1`. The public-scope test (lines 103-111) inspects the mocked client argument only, never the URL, so a regression that re-added the workspace to the public browse URL in the preview path would be invisible.

samples.summary: Upstream-error forwarding and the `seg()` refusal are tested for `publish` only; `list` and `use` error paths are uncovered
samples.evidence: templates.test.ts covers `forwardUpstreamError` only at lines 255-270 (publish) and the traversing-id refusal only at lines 272-282 (publish). The equivalent branches in templates.ts:113 (list) and 194 (use) — plus `templateUseUrl`'s `seg()` at url.ts:148 — have no test, so a `list`/`use` failure printing to stdout or exiting 0 would ship unnoticed.

samples.summary: The three new schema-registry entries have no assertions beyond the generic alias/safety loops, so registry-vs-CLI drift is untested
samples.evidence: schema.test.ts asserts specific names/safety/aliases for docs, sheets, folders, api-keys (lines 128-206, 233-237) but nothing for templates.list/publish/use; the only coverage they get is the generic `all.length > 0` loop (line 119) and the alias-collision check (line 164). Nothing checks that the registry's documented options match the commands registered in templates.ts (e.g. registry declares `--limit` default '24' while the command declares no default, url.ts sends limit as a string).

samples.summary: `expect(query.workspaceId).toBeUndefined()` is the weak assertion form the file's own publish section argues against (it passes on a present key with an undefined value)
samples.evidence: templates.test.ts:110 checks the value rather than the key list, while the publish block (lines 171-184, 206-209) deliberately asserts `Object.keys(...)` for the same class of invariant. Behaviourally harmless here (templateBrowseParams drops undefined), but the assertion does not test what its comment at lines 101-102 claims.

samples.summary: The alias test asserts only that the mock was called once, not that the aliased path behaves identically
samples.evidence: templates.test.ts:160-164 (`accepts the singular \`template\` alias`) asserts `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` with no check of the query or output; it would pass on any alias wiring that reaches the same action with wrong arguments.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. templates.test.ts:23-29 mocks the whole http-client module, so the three new methods at http-client.ts:1151-1176 never run. I searched repo-wide for a counterexample: grep for browseTemplates|publishTemplate|useTemplate|/templates across packages/cli hits only source files plus templates.test.ts; grep for the URL builders (templatesUrl/documentTemplateUrl/templateUseUrl/templateBrowseParams) hits only source and docs, so url.test.ts (which covers seg, workspaceSeg, apiV1Base, apiKeysUrl only) has no template case either; the real-client suites http-client-paths.test.ts and http-client.test.ts drive HttpClient with fetch stubbed for documents/cells/api-keys (incl. the sibling browser route revokeApiKey at lines 76-82) but add no template equivalent; the only other template test in the repo is packages/backend/test/template.e2e-spec.ts, which exercises the server, not the CLI client. The one mitigation I found is that the --dry-run tests run the real url.ts builders (only http-client.js is mocked) and templates.test.ts:272-282 exercises seg()'s dot-segment refusal through documentTemplateUrl — but that verifies the builders, not that the client methods call those builders with the right method/route/body. A publishTemplate that posted to the wrong route or nested the body under the wrong key would pass every existing test while the preview still advertises itself as the request, so the gap is on the live user-facing request path and blocks under the missing-test/over-mocking rubric.
